newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi economy on course for solid 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: Saudi economy on course for solid 1997 growth.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's economy is expected to grow between 2.5-4.5 percent in real terms this year, partly shrugging off a downturn in world oil prices, bankers and economists in the Gulf Arab state said on Wednesday.
Riyadh has enjoyed petrodollar earnings above conservative budget expectations in the first seven months of the year despite a 25 percent fall in world oil prices since January.

But heavy goverment spending, particularly on state salaries, education, health and infrastructure, is likely to keep the budget deficit at around 3.0-3.5 percent of GDP in 1997 and delay plans to balance the budget by the year 2000.
Lower petroleum prices are also expected to return the current account to deficit and rule out a repeat of last year's $12 billion oil windfall.
